title: Iman Gadzhi on his $100M empire: edge-only deals, ecosystems over info, and leading by temperament
summary: Iman explains how he picks investments and businesses only where he has a real edge, why he builds ecosystems and transformation around information, and how he positions his brand by audience stage. He judges everything by revenue, not views, and staffs worst-case thinkers alongside creatives.

principles.text: Only take deals where you can be aggressive on terms and add value; otherwise pass.
principles.quote: if I can't be aggressive, I'm not going to take the deal. If I'm not getting ridiculous, ridiculous terms, I don't take the deal on

principles.text: Without an edge, go passive; don't compete where others are better armed.
principles.quote: So, if I don't have that edge, I'm going to get swept by someone that does have an edge. So, that's why every single Tuesday just cost averaging S&P 500.

principles.text: Don't sell information alone; build ecosystems and tools around the transformation.
principles.quote: I always say you have to build ecosystems inside of info.

principles.text: Judge brand by the business KPI and access to top-tier people, not views.
principles.quote: As long as that's growing or whatever the main KPI is for that business, as long as that's growing and also as long as my exposure to the high high like echelons of people is growing, anything in between I don't really care about.

principles.text: You'll upset someone regardless, so pick your target audience deliberately.
principles.quote: The reality is you're going to piss people off no matter what you do. So, you may as well know who you're targeting.

principles.text: Give worst-case thinkers dedicated roles, and shield creatives from that stress.
principles.quote: And there should be people in your company that are the stressors and are always thinking worst case scenario.
